title: 'CIMB launches 'Lite-i', a no-frills credit card with flexible repayment

title: 'DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share
text:
'DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share

'Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion financing exercise as it moves into the next phase of Malaysia’s 5G development. The financing comes as the nation’s first 5G network has secured a new long-term spectrum assignment, while the government (via MOF Inc) will exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal ownership in DNB. Transition is expected to be completed in early Q4 2026, however, MOF Inc. will retain a special share. DNB completes RM5.2 billion financing DNB said it has completed a RM5.2 billion Syndicated Islamic Term Financing exercise, which it described as among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, while AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank Malaysia were Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing will also be used to refinance DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on 29 September 2026. According to DNB, the new financing provides a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth. The financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s mobile network operator shareholders, based on DNB’s current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets.” He added, “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the Government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” DNB gets 15-year 5G spectrum certainty DNB has also received the full 100MHz block in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, known as F0, while its entire 240MHz spectrum holding has been converted from Apparatus Assignment (AA) into Spectrum Assignment (SA). The Spectrum Assignment for a 15-year period awarded by the MCMC provides greater long-term certainty over spectrum availability and it takes effect from 1 October 2026. title: 'Scientex to Acquire 503 Acres in Johor for RM580 Mil
text:
'Scientex to Acquire 503 Acres in Johor for RM580 Mil

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said in an exchange filing. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. The close proximity between Scientex’s existing projects and the proposed development will generate “better operational efficiencies through greater economies of scale”, the company said. An agreement has been signed between its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd and Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd. Scientex mainly manufactures flexible plastic packaging and develops affordable homes in Malaysia. The company has more than 11,000 acres of land spanning seven states across Peninsular Malaysia in its holdings, according to its website. The company has a goal of building 50,000 affordable homes throughout the nation by 2028 and has delivered 47,000 homes to date. The latest acquisition will be funded through a combination of internal funds and bank borrowings. As of July 31, 2026, Scientex held RM357.8 million in cash against total borrowings of RM2.05 billion. The deal is expected to be closed in the second half of 2027. “The lands are expected to provide a steady and sustainable property development model as Scientex continues to focus on affordably priced landed properties where demand continues to remain firm and resilient,” the company added. Shares of Scientex rose one sen or 0.3% to RM3.61 at Tuesday’s noon break, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM5.6 billion. title: 'Bursa opens in the green — then heavyweight selling takes over
text:
'Bursa opens in the green — then heavyweight selling takes over

'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday but retreated shortly after, weighed down by selling activity in selected heavyweight counters, led by financial services and industrial products and services. At 9.11am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 3.68 points to 1,629.67 from Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The index opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. However, on the broader market, gainers outpaced decliners 221 to 180, with 306 counters unchanged, 2,083 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 327.37 million units worth RM150.56 million. Hong Leong Bank eased 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB slid 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium fell six sen to RM7.13. These three counters collectively pulled down the composite index by a combined 7.23 points. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng noted that Wall Street maintained its positive momentum overnight, with the S&P 500 testing an intra-day record high underpinned by a tech-inspired rally. “This is despite the US 10-year yield remaining elevated at 5.286 per cent while Brent stayed above the US$100 per barrel mark. Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index maintained its uptrend, underpinned by renewed interest in tech-related stocks as sentiment recovered amid the steadying crude oil prices,” he told Bernama. Back home, Thong said he is anticipating bargain-hunting activities to emerge, although any upside may be hampered by selling from foreign funds following the FBM KLCI’s mildly positive close yesterday. “In view of this, we expect the index to continue consolidating within the 1,630-1,640 range today,” he added. Among other heavyweights, AMMB slipped five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. IHH Healthcare added three sen to RM7.94, and Maybank gained two sen to RM9.99. In active trade, Top Glove gained 5.5 sen to 93 sen, and Supermax added 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen, while Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin inched down half a sen each to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively. Metronic Global was flat at half a sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries jumped 62 sen to RM45.58, Nestle gained 32 sen to RM91.58, and Mi Technovation rallied 19 sen to RM6.19. Critical Holdings bounced 12 sen to RM2.81, and Hengyuan Refining Company gained nine sen to RM3.55. Among the top losers, TMK Chemical cut eight sen to RM2.61, and Pekat fell five sen to RM2.91, while Stratus Global and Solarvest slipped four sen each to RM3.09 and RM4.33, respectively. Malaysia Smelting shrank three sen to RM1.65. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 61.25 points to 17,795.36, the FBM Emas Index cut 5.46 points to 12,227.41, and the FBM Top 100 Index lost 9.15 points to 12,006.63. The FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 26.12 points to 12,185.10, and the FBM ACE Index edged up 0.94 points to 5,659.86.

title: 'You can prove the other side was wrong, win the case, and still end up with almost nothing - Newswav
text:
'You can prove the other side was wrong, win the case, and still end up with almost nothing - Newswav

'That is basically what happened in a recent Court of Appeal case. A buyer successfully proved that RHB Bank had wrongly terminated an auction sale. So you might think the next part was easy. The bank was wrong. Pay the buyer. The Sessions Court awarded the buyer RM863,795.37. The High Court agreed. But the Court of Appeal later cancelled almost the entire award and ordered the money to be returned to RHB. Why? Because saying, “You caused me a loss” is not enough. You still have to prove exactly how much you lost. For example, the buyer claimed RM350,000 based on the difference between the property price and a valuation done many years later. The problem was that the breach happened in 2007, but the valuation was from 2020. The buyer also claimed more than 15 years of rental payments. But there were gaps in the documents, and problems showing that all of that rent was actually caused by the bank’s actions. There was also a RM5,000 legal fee claim, but again, there was not enough basis to simply make the bank pay it. The RM26,000 deposit was different. The Court agreed the buyer was entitled to it, but the money had already been sent to the Registrar of Unclaimed Moneys, so it had to be claimed from there. The lesson is simple. Winning the argument is only step one. You must also be able to show: What exactly did you lose? How did you calculate it? Did the other side actually cause that loss? Do you have documents to prove it? Did you do anything to reduce the loss? If you cannot prove those things properly, even a very large damages award can disappear on appeal. Case: RHB Bank Berhad v Tee Ban Tiong, Court of Appeal, decided on 27 August 2026. title: 'Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Twentytwo13
text:
'Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Twentytwo13

'KUALA LUMPUR: Coaches of Premier League hockey teams scheduled to play on Deepavali day are happy they will now battle it out on different dates, as the Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) repeats its 2018 scheduling boo-boo. Two matches – Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces Hockey Team and TNB Thunderbolts versus Maybank – were originally scheduled for Nov 8, the day Deepavali is celebrated in Malaysia. However, the matches will now be rescheduled, much to the delight of TNB Thunderbolts and Terengganu Hockey Team. Mohd Harfizi Baharom of Terengganu said he had been informed that the match against the soldiers would now be played on Nov 9. “It is good that we will not be playing on such an auspicious day. It gives those celebrating the festival time to spend with their families,” Mohd Harfizi told Twentytwo13. “Several of our players have only just returned from the Asian Games. Unfortunately, there is a packed international calendar and the national team will be off to the Asian Champions Trophy from Oct 27 to Nov 5. “As such, having an extra day to prepare for the match against the Armed Forces is welcome. We are third in the standings, but have not given up hope of winning the title. One day can make a difference.” However, the new dates are not reflected on MHC’s website as of publication time. TNB Thunderbolts coach Nor Saiful Zaini, who is also the national junior coach, said he has yet to receive official notice of the new date. “I know it is not easy for MHC to juggle the calendar, but we shouldn’t play on Deepavali or any other religious festival. I am waiting for confirmation regarding the change of date,” said Nor Saiful. In 2018, the Razak Cup was initially scheduled from Nov 3-11, with Deepavali falling on Nov 6 that year. After protests from teams, especially Negeri Sembilan, which threatened to pull out of the tournament, MHC eventually brought forward the tournament to Oct 26-Nov 3. The repeat of the episode raised eyebrows, as those in charge of scheduling the league should have been fully aware of the festive seasons in the country. Meanwhile, Nor Saiful said he would have his hands full as the national juniors will compete in the Sultan of Johor Cup (Oct 17-24), followed by the Murugappa Gold Cup (Oct 25-Nov 4) in India. Nor Saiful was instrumental in recently guiding the national team to next year’s Junior World Cup. “I will need to juggle my team selection carefully, as we have to consider the league matches as well as the two major tournaments. “Some of the teams may be reluctant to release their junior players, but on the bright side, I have the chance to test more players in Johor and India,” he added.

title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
text:
'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential '

KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage.

Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors.

For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information.

“But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said.

He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected.

“These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance.

“For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded.

Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here.

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
text:
'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open '

KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court yesterday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.

Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.

Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.

Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.

In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.

On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.

The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.

The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.

The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.

Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.

The company asserted that this conduct amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.

title: 'Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities
text:
'Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities

'KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets are pricing a more hawkish US Federal Reserve interest rate path than the latest forecasts from policymakers and economists: This could keep the US dollar supported into 2027, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said markets are pricing about 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening in 2027, equivalent to roughly 3.2 rate hikes. This is in comparison with the latest Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) projections for a 25-basis-point increase in the fourth quarter of 2026 and no further hikes in 2027. The FOMC's latest projection puts the policy rate at 4.25 per cent after the expected fourth-quarter move. CIMB Securities said market forecasts for end-2027 rates remain widely dispersed, ranging from 3.25 per cent to 4.50 per cent, with a median of 3.50 per cent. The firm said near-term upside risks to global energy prices and potential price shocks could keep markets positioned for tighter US monetary policy in the fourth quarter of 2026. It also revised higher its forecasts for US Treasury yields relative to German and Japanese government bonds. CIMB Securities raised its end-2027 two-year US Treasury-Bund and US Treasury-JGB spread assumptions by eight basis points and 15 basis points to about 160 basis points and 270 basis points respectively. The wider yield advantage is expected to support the dollar and reduce the case for sustained appreciation in the euro and yen. CIMB Securities said a return of Brent crude to US$100 a barrel could provide another source of support for the dollar, particularly as higher energy prices tend to weigh on currencies of major energy importers. The firm retained its near-term US Dollar Index (DXY) forecast at 101 but raised the third-quarter 2027 projection to 100. However, a decline in Brent below US$90 a barrel could reduce that support, with the DXY ceiling estimated at 99.8 under a lower oil-price scenario. For Asian currencies, CIMB Securities said the impact of higher US rates could be partly offset by relatively stable Chinese yuan conditions and higher regional yields. It expects Asian currencies to remain within their 12-month forecast ranges, with potential yuan strength ahead of a China-US summit providing some stability for the ringgit, Singapore dollar and Thai baht. Higher oil prices and US rates pose greater near-term risks to the Indonesian rupiah, they said, potentially adding pressure for a 25-basis-point Bank Indonesia rate hike in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher On Positive Wall Street Momentum
text:

'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday morning, tracking positive overnight momentum on Wall Street as subdued crude oil prices—driven by a recovery in West Asia crude exports—helped offset a ongoing sell-off in US Treasuries. Meanwhile, ACE Market debutant SLGC fell 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange edged down half a sen to 50 sen. - Top Gainers: Plantation counters saw strong demand, led by Batu Kawan, which surged RM1.24 to RM20.22. title: 'Religious council to bear sisters’ funeral costs after Tambun accident
text:
'Religious council to bear sisters’ funeral costs after Tambun accident

'IPOH: The Perak Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPk) will bear the funeral costs for two sisters who died in a road accident near Taman Perpaduan Ria, Tambun here on Friday (Oct 2). MAIPk chief executive officer Syamsul Hazeman Md Salleh said that the council would also assist their surviving sister, who was hospitalised due to serious injuries from the crash. “The MAIPk will bear the funeral management costs for the two siblings who died, while other forms of assistance for the seriously injured sibling will follow. ALSO READ: Schoolgirls killed in Ipoh crash were sisters, say cops "MAIPk provides funeral management assistance to families who are unable to afford such expenses as well as for the deceased with no next of kin," he said. The two victims - Elyana Nasuha Ibrahim, 19 and her younger sister Suhaila Ibrahim, 10 - were killed at about 7.20am on Friday. Their 12-year-old sister Norhayati Qaliesha Ibrahim, who was riding pillion with her sisters, is being treated at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital for her injuries. ALSO READ: Two schoolgirls killed, one hurt in motorcycle-car crash in Tambun The victims were headed towards Bercham on a motorcycle before being hit by a car that was turning out from a junction onto Jalan Perpaduan. The police are investigating the crash under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. The two sisters were pupils of SK Tasek Dermawan and were orphans living with their older sister in Taman Perpaduan. Following the tragedy, a donation drive has been launched through the school’s Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) to help ease the family’s financial burden. Members of the public wishing to contribute can channel donations to SK Tasek Dermawan’s PTA Maybank account at 508177707877.

title: 'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report
text:
'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report

'TOKYO (Oct 5): A framework for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cooperate with Asian countries on oil stockpiling is set to be launched, with Japan supporting the initiative through financial assistance and stockpiling expertise, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. Saudi, UAE to cooperate in building crude stockpile in Asia, Nikkei reports The Japan-led Asia Zero-Emission Community (Azec), a grouping of 11 countries including Southeast Asian nations, will hold a ministerial meeting in the Philippines on Thursday, where senior Saudi and UAE officials are expected to announce their intention to cooperate on oil stockpiling, the Nikkei said. The framework is expected to be included in a joint statement from the meeting, providing a basis for member countries to discuss expanding oil reserves with Middle Eastern producers, it said Specific details and the scale of cooperation will be worked out through bilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and the UAE possibly expanding exports to participating countries or providing priority supplies in an emergency, Nikkei said Japan already leases domestic private storage tanks to state-owned oil companies in countries such as Saudi Arabia under a joint stockpiling scheme, which Japanese companies can access in an emergency Japan is expected to share the framework at a ministerial dialogue of the International Energy Forum in Saudi Arabia on Oct 11, the report said. A Japanese industry ministry official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there will be dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the UAE and oil-consuming countries in Asia on the sidelines of the Azec ministerial meeting, although no concrete projects will be discussed. title: '默迪卡118发展完成 PNB放眼经常收入达6亿 | e南洋
text:
'默迪卡118发展完成 PNB放眼经常收入达6亿 | e南洋

'（吉隆坡5日讯）国民投资机构（PNB）子公司PNB Merdeka Ventures私人有限公司（PNBMV）预计，随着默迪卡118（Merdeka 118）发展项目完成，中期每年可取得约5亿至6亿令吉的经常性收入。 根据大马评级机构MARC点出，默迪卡118办公楼约70%的空间已转租。PNBMV已将办公楼整体以“三重净租赁”方式出租予母公司PNB，因此可降低办公楼空置率及大部分房地产相关成本风险。 默迪卡118办公楼拥有约160万平方尺净可出租面积，其中约40%，即33层，已转租予马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主板金融股），约20%出租予PNB，另约10%出租予其他租户。 MARC预计，办公楼出租率未来5年可提高至约90%，每年净房地产收入料达1亿3700万令吉。 与此同时，MARC已确认PNBMV总值60亿令吉的默迪卡伊斯兰债券获AAAIS评级，展望稳定。 该评级与PNB的AAA／稳定企业信用评级一致，主要受到PNB提供无条件及不可撤销滚动担保的支持，以弥补伊斯兰债券本金及利润支付的任何短缺。 至于预计下月开业的7层楼零售商场，目前已有或正在洽谈的租赁协议覆盖约81%的75万324平方尺净可出租面积，指示性平均租金为每平方尺11.92令吉。 值得注意的是，马银行已正式进驻默迪卡118，而这座吉隆坡地标也已易名为“马银行默迪卡大楼”（Menara Merdeka Maybank）。

title: 'Nanta titip pesanan buat Syed Saddiq, Bella-‘Perkahwinan umpama jalan raya’
text:
'Nanta titip pesanan buat Syed Saddiq, Bella-‘Perkahwinan umpama jalan raya’

'MENTERI Kerja Raya Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi berkongsikan pertemuannya dengan bakal pengantin Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan selebriti Bella Astillah.  Namun, apa yang lebih menarik nasihat dititipkan Nanta terhadap pasangan dua sejoli itu yang sedang menghitung hari untuk bergelar raja sehari.  Pesanan Nanta kepada pasangan berkenaan agak menarik apabila menyifatkan perkahwinan “seumpama jalan raya”.  “Bila berjumpa orang muda yang bakal melangkah ke alam perkahwinan, sempatlah saya kongsi sedikit pesanan.  “Saya kata, perkahwinan ni umpama jalan raya — mesti dua hala, tak boleh sehala. Kena saling memberi, saling menerima dan sama-sama bertolak ansur.  “Dalam rumah tangga, bukan soal siapa betul atau siapa menang. Yang penting, dua-dua kena tahu bila nak jalan, bila nak berhenti, dan kadang-kadang bila kena bagi laluan,” katanya dalam hantaran di Facebooknya.  Nanta turut mendoakan agar segala urusan Syed Saddiq dan Bella dipermudahkan dan semoga perjalanan yang bakal ditempuh bersama nanti sentiasa diberkati dan dipenuhi kebahagiaan.  Syed Saddiq dan Bella dijadualkan akan melangsungkan akad nikah pada 10 Oktober ini di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur.- MalaysiaPost

title: 'Maybank lengkap ambil alih baki 30.95 peratus ekuiti Maybank Ageas
text:
'Maybank lengkap ambil alih baki 30.95 peratus ekuiti Maybank Ageas

'PETALING JAYA: Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) melengkapkan cadangan pengambilalihan baki kepentingan 30.95 peratus dalam Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad selepas menandatangani perjanjian pembelian saham (SPA) bersama Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas). Pengambilalihan itu disempurnakan menyusuli kelulusan kawal selia yang diterima daripada Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) bagi membolehkan MAHB kini beroperasi sebagai anak syarikat milik penuh Maybank. Maybank Ageas merupakan syarikat pegangan bagi perniagaan Etiqa di Malaysia dan Singapura yang menyediakan rangkaian lengkap produk insurans hayat dan am konvensional serta takaful keluarga dan am. Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Maybank, Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli berkata, pencapaian itu merupakan mercu tanda penting bagi Maybank dalam usaha memperkukuh aspirasi Etiqa untuk menjadi peneraju insurans dan takaful nasional serta organisasi bertaraf global di bawah strategi ROAR30. “Dengan Maybank Ageas kini menjadi anak syarikat milik penuh, kedudukan Etiqa sebagai peneraju insurans dan takaful nasional semakin kukuh, sekali gus memperluas capaian kepada pangkalan pelanggan Maybank. “Fokus kami adalah untuk memacu nilai kepada pelanggan di seluruh Asia Tenggara melalui tawaran kekayaan serantau, strategi jualan silang serta penyediaan penyelesaian kewangan yang lebih bersepadu,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Menurut beliau, pemilikan penuh itu turut mengukuhkan penciptaan nilai jangka panjang yang mampan menerusi pengurusan modal yang lebih berkesan dan cekap di peringkat Kumpulan Maybank. “Jenama Etiqa kekal sebagai francais insurans dan takaful yang kukuh dan akan terus diletakkan sebagai salah satu jenama utama Maybank. “Kami juga ingin merakamkan penghargaan kepada Ageas atas kerjasama selama 25 tahun bersama Maybank serta sumbangan mereka dalam membangunkan francais Etiqa,” tambahnya. Maybank Ageas berada pada kedudukan kukuh untuk memanfaatkan peluang pertumbuhan dalam sektor insurans dan takaful menerusi pangkalan pelanggan yang besar serta rangkaian pengedaran menyeluruh Kumpulan. Langkah berkenaan turut membolehkan Maybank dan Maybank Ageas meningkatkan keupayaan bagi memacu inovasi produk, memperluas penembusan insurans perbankan dan memperkukuh tawaran takaful di samping meningkatkan kecekapan operasi. – UTUSAN

title: 'Maybank limits BTS world tour debit card to 60 per branch per day, online applications open 28 September
text:
'Maybank limits BTS world tour debit card to 60 per branch per day, online applications open 28 September

'Subscribe to our FREE Newsletter, or Telegram and WhatsApp channels for the latest stories and updates.  Maybank dropped the limited-edition Maybank Visa BTS World Tour “ARIRANG” Debit Card at 12 selected branches yesterday, and just as expected, fans queued up in droves to get their hands on it!  The new black card has a simple design, with the words “BTS World Tour ARIRANG” printed in a glossy finish across the bottom half of the card. It was released in conjunction with the Kpop band’s upcoming world tour.  Fans who braved the queues outside the banks proudly shared pictures of their new cards online. It’s easy to see why the excitement is so real because only 60 cards are issued per day at each selected Maybank branch, making this a seriously hot commodity.  If you don’t have time to queue, you can still get your hands on the Maybank BTS card online via Maybank2U from 28 September onwards. Simply open the Maybank2U app, go to “Settings,” select “Cards,” then choose “Replace/Renew Card.” Do note that this process comes with a card replacement fee of RM12.  Excitement for BTS-themed cards abroad  Malaysian fans are not the only ones treated to a special BTS bank card. Fans in Thailand and the Philippines have also shared their respective country’s card designs online — a sign of just how deeply the group has embedded itself across Southeast Asia.  That footprint runs especially deep in Malaysia. BTS has consistently sold out arenas here since their early tour years, with Malaysian ARMY widely regarded as one of the most organised and vocal fandoms in the region. The group’s blend of polished choreography, emotionally direct lyrics, and members who have spoken openly about mental health resonated strongly with young Malaysians navigating similar pressures. The fact that a national bank is now issuing limited-edition BTS debit cards is, in many ways, just the financial sector catching up to what fans already knew.  An Indonesian fan on X, formerly Twitter, expressed hope that local banks would release a BTS-themed card — or at minimum, a Flazz card, an e-money smart card issued by Bank Central Asia. The comment drew significant engagement, suggesting the appetite extends well beyond Malaysia’s borders.  Share your thoughts with us via TRP’s Facebook, X, Instagram, or Threads.
